findings.description: The regex captures only the first find root and silently consumes additional roots. For `find ./build / -exec rm -rf {} +`, the safety check classifies only the allow-listed `./build`, although find also traverses `/`.
findings.failure_mode: A destructive invocation covering a protected second root can pass the safety hook and recursively delete files outside the allowed directory.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore rejection of multiple roots, or parse and validate every find root before allowing the rm invocation.

findings.description: Removing billing-error classification makes account credit exhaustion returned as HTTP 400 a terminal InvalidInputError. The same regression exists in _complete_nonstreaming.
findings.failure_mode: Requests stop at an exhausted Anthropic account instead of invoking the configured provider fallback, even when a usable fallback is available.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve ProviderUnavailableError classification for billing and account-quota errors in both transport paths, while keeping request-validation errors terminal.

findings.description: The completed count now includes historical sprint directories outside the current plan, while determine_state still compares it against the sprint count in the current sprint.md. For a two-sprint plan, two historical COMPLETED markers suffice even if neither planned sprint is complete.
findings.failure_mode: The workflow reports complete and recommends /deploy-production while current implementation, review, or audit work remains unfinished.
findings.suggested_fix: Count only completion markers belonging to the current plan or active cycle, using the same sprint set for both completed and total counts.

findings.description: Iterating over unquoted ${sprint_dirs} splits each absolute path on whitespace. A checkout under a directory such as `/home/user/My Project` therefore fails to recognize its existing COMPLETED markers.
findings.failure_mode: Completed sprints are reported as zero; a fully completed plan can consequently be reported as sprint_planned with a recommendation to implement sprint-1 again.
findings.suggested_fix: Read find results using a NUL-delimited loop with `IFS= read -r -d ''`, keeping each directory path intact.

findings.description: The new regex captures only the FIRST non-space token after `find` as the root (`[^;&|)[:space:]]+`) and line 807 assigns it directly, replacing the old tokeniser that counted leading non-flag tokens and refused (root="") when the count was not exactly 1. GNU/BSD find accept multiple starting points: every argument before the first one beginning with `-`, `(`, `!` or `,` is a root. For `find ./build / -exec rm -rf {} +` the hook now resolves `{}` against `./build` only, ignores `/`, and if `./build` is on the allow-list the rm segment is permitted while the real command recursively deletes from `/`. The old implementation mirrored find's path-parsing rule and was fail-closed on this input; the new one is fail-open.
findings.failure_mode: Any `find ALLOWED_ROOT DANGEROUS_ROOT ... -exec rm ...` command bypasses the safety hook. Catastrophic recursive deletion (e.g. of `/`, `$HOME`, or a sibling repo) is allowed because only the first root is classified.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the first-token capture for the common case but preserve the multi-root guard: after matching, re-tokenise the span between `find` and `-exec` (the old `read -r -a` loop) and set `_seg_find_root=""` whenever more than one leading non-flag token exists. Alternatively, make the regex require that the token immediately following the root starts with `-`, `(`, `!` or `,` (e.g. `find[[:space:]]+([^;&|)[:space:]-]+)[[:space:]]+([-(!,][^;&|)]*)?-exec$`) so a second root fails the match and falls back to the conservative path. Add a fixture `find ./build / -exec rm -rf {} +` → BLOCK.

findings.description: The comment claims `find -L root -exec ...` 'keeps today's conservative behavior', but with the new regex the captured root becomes the literal flag `-L` (or `-name`, `-maxdepth` etc. for `find -name x -exec ...` where find defaults to `.`). Previously the tokeniser broke on the leading `-*` token and yielded root="". The downstream path now receives a flag string as a root, which is a different code path (reviewer notes it lands in FR-2-AMBIGUOUS) than the documented one. Outcome currently still blocks, but the comment misdescribes the mechanism and any future allow-list entry or normalisation that treats a leading `-` token leniently would silently flip this to allow.
findings.failure_mode: Future maintainers rely on the comment, assume root="" semantics for flag-first invocations, and introduce a fail-open when the actual root value is `-L`/`-name`.
findings.suggested_fix: Either exclude `-`-prefixed first tokens from the capture (`([^;&|)[:space:]-][^;&|)[:space:]]*)`) so flag-first `find` falls back to root="" as before, or rewrite the comment to state that flag-first invocations yield a flag-shaped root that routes to the ambiguous/block arm.

findings.cross_file_justification: The diff deletes module-level symbols `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` and `_is_billing_class_error` from anthropic_adapter.py. The existing test module `.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_adapter_billing_class.py` imports `_is_billing_class_error` from this module and is not touched by the diff.
findings.description: `_is_billing_class_error` and `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` are removed without updating or deleting the test module that imports them. `from loa_cheval.providers.anthropic_adapter import _is_billing_class_error` raises ImportError at collection time, failing the whole test file (9 tests) and the CI run, not just the billing-specific assertions.
findings.failure_mode: Test suite collection error / CI red on merge; any downstream module that imported the helper fails at import time.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete or rewrite `.claude/adapters/tests/test_anthropic_adapter_billing_class.py` in the same PR (grep the repo for `_is_billing_class_error` and `_BILLING_CLASS_TOKENS` to catch any other importers). If the classifier is intentionally removed, replace the tests with ones asserting the new terminal-InvalidInputError behaviour for billing-shaped 4xx bodies.

findings.description: Both the streaming (lines 139-141) and non-streaming (`_complete_nonstreaming`, lines 221-223) paths now raise terminal `InvalidInputError` for every non-429 4xx, including account-side billing conditions (credit balance exhausted, quota_exceeded, invoice_overdue, billing_disabled). The deleted helper's docstring and the retry layer contract were that billing-class errors are `ProviderUnavailableError` so the within-company chain walks to the next provider (e.g. claude-headless). After this change a billing failure on the API-key provider is terminal and the fallback chain is never consulted, even though an alternative transport is configured and healthy. No replacement classification is introduced elsewhere in the diff.
findings.failure_mode: Operator's account hits a credit/quota limit → every request fails fast with InvalidInputError instead of failing over; the redundancy the chain was built for is silently disabled. Also a behavioural regression against the documented known-failure handling without a CHANGELOG or ADR entry.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep the billing-class → ProviderUnavailableError mapping (ideally in `types.py`/`base.py` so all adapters share it) or, if removal is intentional, document the decision, update the retry/chain contract, and ensure the retry layer treats these 4xx errors as chain-walkable by another mechanism (e.g. status-code based: 402/403 with `billing`/`credit` error type).

findings.description: `get_completed_sprints` now counts every `a2a/sprint-*/COMPLETED` directory on disk instead of only `sprint-1..N` where N comes from the current `sprint.md`. `determine_state` (unchanged) still compares this count against `get_total_sprints` and returns `complete` when `completed >= total`. With a2a dirs left over from a previous cycle (e.g. sprint-4..sprint-8 COMPLETED) and a new sprint.md with 3 sprints none of which are finished, the count is 5 ≥ 3 and the script reports state `complete`, progress 95%, and suggests `/deploy-production` while the actual sprints are not started. The glob `sprint-*` also matches `sprint-3-archived`, `sprint-foo`, etc. The per-sprint loop in `determine_state` and `main` still iterates `sprint-1..total`, so the two sources of truth now disagree.
findings.failure_mode: Wrong workflow state and wrong suggested next command (`/deploy-production`) whenever stale or renamed a2a sprint directories exist, which is the normal condition after any cycle rollover. Result is cached, so the error persists until prd/sdd/sprint.md mtime changes.
findings.suggested_fix: Bound the count to the current plan: either restore the `1..total` loop, or intersect the found dirs with `sprint-[0-9]+` and `i <= total` (`[[ "$dir" =~ /sprint-([0-9]+)$ ]] && (( BASH_REMATCH[1] <= total ))`). If cross-cycle historical counting is genuinely wanted, expose it as a separate function/field and leave `determine_state`'s comparison on the bounded count.

findings.description: `for dir in ${sprint_dirs}` word-splits the newline-separated `find` output on IFS (space/tab/newline) and glob-expands each word. A grimoire path containing a space (e.g. a project under `~/My Projects/`) splits each directory into fragments, so `[[ -f "${dir}/COMPLETED" ]]` never matches and the count is 0. `dir` is also not declared `local` and leaks into the global scope.
findings.failure_mode: Completed-sprint count is always 0 on repositories whose path contains whitespace; progress and state regress to `implementing sprint-1`.
findings.suggested_fix: Use `while IFS= read -r dir; do ...; done < <(find "${a2a_dir}" -maxdepth 1 -type d -name 'sprint-*' 2>/dev/null)` or a quoted glob (`for dir in "${a2a_dir}"/sprint-*/; do [[ -d "$dir" ]] || continue; ...`) and declare `local dir`.
